name: Christian Dior SE
reason: Holding company for ~41% of LVMH with a strong luxury franchise, but EPS has fallen from EUR 34.93 (2023) to 25.10 (0.72x peak) in a luxury/China demand downturn, 10y EPS CAGR is only 6.7% and there is no NTM consensus, so the recovery path cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Telefonica Deutschland Holding AG
reason: Mature, now Telefonica-controlled German mobile operator with 0.4% 10y revenue CAGR, EBIT margin of only 3.3% and adjusted EPS of EUR 0.05 in 2023 (data stops after squeeze-out), so no route to 7%+ EPS growth.

name: Star Bulk Carriers Corp.
reason: Dry-bulk shipowner whose earnings track freight rates (EBIT margin -33% to 52% over 10y, EPS 0.14x its 2021 peak of USD 6.82) and whose share count rose 11.4%/yr; commodity-cycle earner.

name: HelloFresh SE
reason: Meal-kit retailer with negative 10y average ROIC (-12.7%), adjusted EPS down from EUR 2.09 (2020) to 0.45 and EBIT margin around zero; weak, non-durable economics.

name: CMB.TECH NV
reason: Tanker/dry-bulk shipping group with freight-rate-driven earnings (EBIT margin -73% to 47%), 10y EPS CAGR of -11.6% and net debt/EBITDA of 7.4x after the Golden Ocean merger; cyclical and leveraged.

name: TeamViewer SE
reason: Profitable remote-access software (EBIT margin 32%, adjusted EPS EUR 0.56 to 1.17 since 2019), but the debt-funded 1E acquisition took net debt to 3.0x EBITDA, adjusted EPS is ~54% above GAAP, consensus FY1 is -15.5% and organic growth has slowed amid competition and AI-agent risk.

name: Jupiter Fund Management plc
reason: Active UK asset manager in structural outflows: adjusted EPS fell from GBP 0.29 (2015) to 0.19 (-4.0%/yr) and EBIT margin from 42% to 27.5%; market-driven and not special.

name: Avolta AG
reason: Concession-based travel retailer whose growth came from acquisitions (Autogrill) with shares up 11.6%/yr, EPS of CHF 3.41 still half the 2018 level of 6.90, negative 10y average ROIC and net debt/EBITDA of 3.7x.

name: Teleperformance SE
reason: Labour-based CX/BPO outsourcer facing a direct AI-automation threat, with growth bought via acquisitions (0.84x 10y FCF, Majorel/LanguageLine) and consensus EPS growth of only 2-5% from EUR 13.20; consistent with CNXC (NO).

name: DNO ASA
reason: Oil and gas producer (Kurdistan, North Sea) whose earnings are set by commodity prices and Kurdish export politics; EPS has swung from USD -0.29 to 0.43 and was negative in 2025.

name: ANIMA Holding S.p.A.
reason: Italian retail asset manager, now controlled by Banco BPM, whose fees track market levels and flows; EPS of EUR 0.90 at 1.0x its 10y max with EBIT margin at a 10y high (27.5%) and consensus FY2 -5.5%; capital-markets earner without specialness.

name: Prosegur Cash SA
reason: Cash-in-transit operator exposed to the secular decline of cash and LatAm currency translation, with adjusted EPS down from EUR 0.12 (2018) to 0.06 and EBIT margin from 19.5% to 9.9%.

name: Odfjell Drilling Ltd.
reason: Offshore rig owner whose earnings depend on oil-cycle dayrates; EBIT margin at the 91st pctile of history (29.9%) and 10y average ROIC of 4.1%.

name: Deutsche Telekom AG
reason: Controls T-Mobile US (US KEEP), a share-taking member of a 3-player wireless oligopoly, plus a stable German incumbent; adjusted EPS rose from EUR 0.79 to 2.00 (9.8% CAGR, 6/10 years >=7%) with consensus 10-14% for FY1-FY3 and net debt/EBITDA of 2.6x; USD translation and the ~28% German state stake are watch items.

name: Peugeot Invest SA
reason: Investment holding company whose earnings are dividends and gains on listed stakes (Stellantis, Forvia) and private equity; EPS of EUR 8.75 is lower than 2014 (12.23) and 10y average ROE is 4.6%.

name: Sonae SGPS SA
reason: Family-controlled Portuguese retail conglomerate with a 3.8% EBIT margin, 10y average ROIC of 4.8%, net debt/EBITDA 3.1x and 10y EPS CAGR of 4.6% (EUR 0.08 to 0.12); ordinary economics.

name: Vonovia SE
reason: Rate-sensitive German residential landlord with FFO/share down from EUR 2.42 (2022) to 1.77, net debt/EBITDA of 17x, acquisition-led growth (3.0x FCF) and shares up 7.1%/yr; consensus is about 0-3%/yr.

name: Aker Solutions ASA
reason: Oilfield engineering and services contractor tied to Norwegian offshore capex; EPS of NOK 5.46 at 1.0x its 10y max with consensus FY2 -40.8%, and 10y average ROIC of 4.3%.

name: Basic-Fit NV
reason: Low-cost gym chain with a clear value proposition, but unlike asset-light PLNT it owns and leases its clubs and funds rollout and the Clever Fit deal with debt (net debt/EBITDA 4.9x, shares +7.9%/yr, 10y average ROIC -1.6%), and adjusted EPS of EUR 0.81 is far above GAAP.

name: Hbx Group International Plc
reason: B2B hotel bedbank (Hotelbeds) only listed in 2025 with GAAP losses every year since 2022 (EPS EUR -0.28 in 2025), net debt/EBITDA 2.1x and AI/direct-booking disintermediation risk; the record is too short to forecast.
